question_text: For a standard domestic First-Class Mail letter, what is the maximum weight allowed for the letter category?
correct_answer: The maximum weight is 3.5 ounces for a First-Class Mail letter.
incorrect_answer: The maximum weight is 4.5 ounces for a First-Class Mail letter.
source_citation: USPS, Letters: Size and Weight Standards
ground_truth_note: The USPS letter standards state that First-Class Mail letters can weigh up to 3.5 ounces.

question_text: For domestic Media Mail, what is the usual delivery timeframe listed for the service?
correct_answer: The usual delivery timeframe is 2 to 8 business days.
incorrect_answer: The usual delivery timeframe is 3 to 10 business days.
ground_truth_note: The USPS service listing gives Media Mail an expected delivery timeframe of 2 to 8 business days.

question_text: For domestic Ground Advantage retail shipments, how much insurance is generally included at no extra charge?
correct_answer: Up to $100 of insurance is generally included at no extra charge.
incorrect_answer: Up to $50 of insurance is generally included at no extra charge.
ground_truth_note: The USPS Ground Advantage page states that the service includes up to $100 of insurance.

question_text: For an open-end credit card account, how far before the due date must the issuer generally send or deliver a periodic statement for grace-period protections to apply?
correct_answer: The issuer generally must send or deliver the statement at least 21 days before the due date.
incorrect_answer: The issuer generally must send or deliver the statement at least 14 days before the due date.
ground_truth_note: Regulation Z requires periodic statements to be sent or delivered at least 21 days before the payment due date for grace-period protections.

question_text: Under federal funds-availability rules, how much of a check deposit must a bank generally make available by the next business day?
correct_answer: The bank generally must make the first $225 available by the next business day.
incorrect_answer: The bank generally must make the first $200 available by the next business day.
source_citation: CFPB, Ask CFPB: I deposited a check. When will my funds be available?
ground_truth_note: The CFPB explains that banks generally must make the first $225 from a check deposit available by the next business day.

question_text: For a routine U.S. passport application, what processing timeframe is generally listed, not counting mailing time?
correct_answer: Routine processing is generally listed as 4 to 6 weeks, not counting mailing time.
incorrect_answer: Routine processing is generally listed as 6 to 8 weeks, not counting mailing time.
ground_truth_note: The State Department passport processing page lists routine processing as 4 to 6 weeks, excluding mailing time.

question_text: What federal additional tax generally applies to an IRA distribution taken before age 59½ when no exception applies?
correct_answer: A 10% additional tax generally applies to the early distribution.
incorrect_answer: A 15% additional tax generally applies to the early distribution.
source_citation: IRS Topic No. 557, Additional Tax on Early Distributions from Traditional and Roth IRAs
ground_truth_note: IRS Topic No. 557 states that early IRA distributions are generally subject to a 10% additional tax unless an exception applies.

question_text: After receiving a COBRA election notice for job-based health coverage, how long does a qualified beneficiary generally have to elect COBRA continuation coverage?
correct_answer: The beneficiary generally has 60 days to elect COBRA continuation coverage.
incorrect_answer: The beneficiary generally has 30 days to elect COBRA continuation coverage.
source_citation: DOL, Continuation of Health Coverage: COBRA
ground_truth_note: The Department of Labor explains that qualified beneficiaries must generally be given at least 60 days to elect COBRA coverage.

question_text: After the IRS mails a notice of deficiency to a taxpayer in the United States, how long does the taxpayer generally have to file a petition with the U.S. Tax Court?
correct_answer: The taxpayer generally has 90 days to file a petition with the U.S. Tax Court.
incorrect_answer: The taxpayer generally has 60 days to file a petition with the U.S. Tax Court.
source_citation: U.S. Tax Court, Starting a Case
ground_truth_note: The U.S. Tax Court explains that a petition generally must be filed within 90 days after the notice of deficiency is mailed.

question_text: For someone first eligible for Medicare at age 65, what is the usual Initial Enrollment Period for Part B?
correct_answer: It runs for seven months, from three months before through three months after the month the person turns 65.
incorrect_answer: It runs for five months, from two months before through two months after the month the person turns 65.
source_citation: Medicare.gov, When does Medicare coverage start?
ground_truth_note: Medicare.gov describes the Initial Enrollment Period as a seven-month period surrounding the month a person turns 65.

question_text: At the federal level, when does a U.S. person generally have to file an FBAR for foreign financial accounts?
correct_answer: When the aggregate value of foreign financial accounts exceeded $10,000 at any time during the calendar year.
incorrect_answer: When the aggregate value of foreign financial accounts exceeded $50,000 at the end of the calendar year.
source_citation: IRS, Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts
ground_truth_note: The IRS states that an FBAR is generally required when aggregate foreign financial accounts exceed $10,000 at any time during the calendar year.

question_text: Under federal rules, if a consumer reports a lost debit card within two business days after learning of the loss, what is the maximum loss for unauthorized transfers?
correct_answer: The consumer’s maximum loss is generally $50.
incorrect_answer: The consumer’s maximum loss is generally $500.
source_citation: FTC Consumer Advice, Lost or Stolen Credit, ATM, and Debit Cards
ground_truth_note: The FTC explains that reporting a lost debit card within two business days generally limits the consumer’s loss to $50.
